title: Lease Term Agreement Terms — Notice to Vacate, Withdrawal and Move-Out Date
content:
A notice to vacate on a Lease Term Agreement is the resident's written statement of the date they will give up the apartment home at or after the end of the term.

## Section 1 — Recording a notice

1.1 **Written notice.** A notice to vacate is recorded only from the resident's own written notice through a channel accepted for notices (the resident portal or a signed notice form); a verbal statement of plans is not notice. This rests on the resident's own statement and is recorded against the resident's current term.

1.2 On a fixed term the intended move-out date must be on or after the term end date — an earlier date is an early termination or lease break, never a notice. On a month-to-month agreement any date may be given.

## Section 2 — Insufficient notice

2.1 When the intended move-out date is earlier than the notice date plus the program's notice-to-vacate days, the notice is still recorded and an insufficient notice charge is assessed for the days short; the resident may instead move the date out to avoid it.

2.2 The charge is computed on the daily contracted rent: the contracted rent multiplied by 12 and divided by 365, rounded half up to the cent per day, multiplied by the days short.

*Worked example (hypothetical).* Contracted rent 1,825.00 dollars on a program requiring 60 days; notice received on a date giving only 50 days before the intended move-out date. Daily rent: 1,825.00 multiplied by 12 is 21,900.00, divided by 365 is 60.00. Days short: 10. Charge: 600.00 dollars.

## Section 3 — Changing the move-out date

A resident on notice may move the intended date later only up to the day before any new lease on the same apartment home starts, and earlier only if the new date still satisfies the rules above.

## Section 4 — Withdrawing a notice

4.1 **Withdrawal window.** A notice may be withdrawn only when the current date is no later than the date the notice to vacate was received plus the program's withdrawal window days. Withdrawal days are counted as calendar days starting the day after the notice was received, and the last counted day is included. The received date is the notice date on the term record.

4.2 Withdrawal also requires that the program allows withdrawal and that no other lease has been applied for or approved on the same apartment home; withdrawing removes any insufficient notice charge by a charge reversal.

| Hypothetical: notice received 10 April, withdrawal window 14 days | Result |
|---|---|
| Counted days | 11 April through 24 April |
| Withdrawal asked on 24 April, no other lease applied for | May be withdrawn |
| Withdrawal asked on 25 April | May not be withdrawn |
| Withdrawal asked on 20 April, another lease already approved on the apartment home | May not be withdrawn |

## Section 5 — End of the term

The term completes when possession ends; a resident who stays beyond the intended move-out date owes holdover rent under the term charge rule.
